description: A field does not move more than 3× from one fiscal year to the next.
Capex ÷ revenue stays within 2× of the company's own median for the window.
The same field and period read from two filings gives two different values.
The row a field is read from has the same label in every filing for a company.
The line read for a field says it covers more (or less) than the field's definition.
The value matches XBRL within the coarser rounding of the two sources.
Names the years no 10-K can show, and any company with no 10-K at all, so a gap is never silent.
When a company reports no total cost-of-revenue line, the cost lines an agent classified as cost of revenue were added up; the rule lists them.
Every agent value cites a table, row, column and cell that exist in the parsed filing, and the cell × unit (with the field's sign rule) equals the value.
The cited column's label agrees with the period the value claims (end date or year, and length).
Every released field has a value (or a stated reason) for every fiscal year in the window. A year after the newest 10-K is not missing until that year's 10-K is due (90 days after the year ends).
Each value read from a 10-K covers one fiscal year.
Revenue, capex and opex are never negative.
In each income statement: revenue − cost of revenue − total operating expenses = operating income, in every column.
The unit (thousands, millions) was not stated with the table and was taken from elsewhere in the same filing.
